paragraphs: God, remember everything we've been through. Take a good look at our situation, at the shameful mark we've left on history. Our precious land has been handed over to outsiders, our homes to strangers. We're orphans with no father in sight, and our mothers are no better off than widows. We have to pay just to drink our own water. Even our firewood costs us money.

We've become nothing but slaves—bullied, beaten down, worn out with no rest in sight. We sold ourselves to Assyria and Egypt just to get something to eat. Our parents sinned and they're gone now, and we're the ones paying for what they did. Slaves are ruling over us, and there's no escaping their grip. We risk our lives just to find food out in the desert where bandits roam.

Our skin has turned black like the inside of an oven, dried out like old leather from the famine. Our wives were assaulted in the streets of Zion, our young women in the towns of Judah. They hanged our princes by their hands and showed no respect to our elders. Strong young men were forced to do women's work, and little boys had to do the work of grown men.

The city gate sits empty—no wise elders there anymore. You can't hear music from the young people anymore. All the joy has drained out of our hearts. Our dancing has turned into funeral songs. The crown of glory has fallen off our heads. Oh no, oh no—if only we had never sinned! Because of all this, we're heartsick. We can't even see through our tears. Mount Zion lies wrecked and ruined, with wild animals prowling through it.

And yet, God, you're still in charge. Your throne is solid and lasts forever. So why do you keep forgetting about us? Why have you abandoned us like this? Bring us back to you, God—we're ready to come home. Give us a fresh start. Because right now, it feels like you've cruelly disowned us. You've been so angry with us.

title: Give Us a Fresh Start
